name: Dusty khaki
lede: Dusty khaki is a pale, greyed yellow-green, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Urahayanagi, "the underside of willow leaves."

sections.title: The underside of a willow leaf
sections.body:
Urahayanagi (裏柳) is listed among Japan's traditional colors on Wikipedia, where the kanji translate as "underside of willow leaves," the paler, more silvery face of the leaf compared with its darker top side [1]. No date for the name is given in the sources consulted, so its age here is undocumented [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[yellowish-grey]] and [[sand]], at 3 and 3.8 ΔE [3]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[misty-moss]], 4.8 ΔE away, more vivid [3]. Further out still, [[asparagus-green]] sits 4.1 ΔE away, almost the same [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 2,156 of 23,781 paintings, about 9.1 percent, as photographed [2]. It is most common in a sample of 416 paintings from the 1770s, where it appears in 56, about one and a half times the archive's overall rate for that decade [2]. Among sampled painters, Alexander von Kotzebue's twelve paintings contain it in eight, the highest rate recorded [2]. It also shows up above average in paintings from Iran, Tibet, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].

openers: Named for the pale side of a willow leaf, turned away from the sun.
